# Josie Pye

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006)</sub>
- **Origin:** Avonlea  <sub>[v1 c38 P40](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0040), [v3 c16 P2](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0002)</sub>
- **Role:** Student  <sub>[v1 c30 P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006)</sub>

## Appearance

Josie Pye is stout or fat in build. She is described as looking flushed or defiant at times.

_Sources: [v1 c23 P6](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0006), [v1 c24 P14](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0014)_

## Personality

Josie is sharp-tongued, disagreeable, and sulky when she does not get her way. She is envious of others' achievements and prone to malicious, spiteful gossip. She can also be cheat-like in school competitions and holds a boastful and triumphant attitude when successful.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P25](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0025), [v1 c23 P6](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0006), [v1 c24 P14](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0014), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v1 c37 P33](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0033), [v3 c16 P2](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0002)_

## Goals

- going to college for education's sake without needing to earn a living  <sub>[v1 c30 P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021)</sub>

## History

Josie attended Avonlea school under Mr. Phillips and later Miss Stacy. During her school days, she was caught peeping in her book during a spelling exercise by Anne Shirley. At a gathering, she successfully walked the top of the Barry garden board fence after performing a dare, triumphing over the other girls. She caused friction among her classmates when she became sulky over not getting the role of the fairy queen in a local concert dialogue, and later stopped speaking with Julia Bell for three months after making a derogatory comment about Julia's recitation bow. At the Exhibition, Josie earned first prize for her knitted lace. She eventually joined the Queen's class to study for college, noting that she was pursuing higher education purely for education's sake rather than out of financial necessity. While at Queen's Academy, she maintained a reputation as the sharpest-tongued student. When Anne Shirley's prize story was published later on, Josie spitefully claimed that Anne had merely copied it from an old paper.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P25](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0025), [v1 c23 P6](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0006), [v1 c24 P14](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0014), [v1 c26 P2](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0002), [v1 c29 P24](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0024), [v1 c30 P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v3 c16 P2](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0002)_
